subject: English First Additional Language
source: DBE Annual Teaching Plan 2023/24 — check for a newer version before use.

weeks.narrative: Learners complete the standardised baseline assessment over the first three days. Learners then listen to an article from a brochure read aloud, organise its information and discuss the brochure's features and diction.

Learners read a brochure for format, target audience, layout, language and purpose. Introduce poetry: internal and external structure, figurative meaning, mood and theme. Learners write and design a brochure using process writing.

Learners listen to a multimedia text on creating an email, then record main and supporting ideas by note-making, summarising and paraphrasing. Task 1 Oral (Reading Aloud, 20 marks) starts this term and is completed in Term 2.

Learners read an email for comprehension by skimming, scanning and intensive reading, noting purpose, target group and the impact of fonts. Introduce folklore features. Learners write an email in the correct format and style.

Teach a group discussion on the novel: learners brainstorm and sequence main ideas and do listening comprehension in preparation for summary writing. Introduce the youth novel's character, plot, conflict, setting and theme.

Teach the principles of summary writing and pre-reading strategies such as text features and parts of a book. Learners write a narrative or reflective essay using process writing. Task 2: Writing, essay, 30 marks.

Learners prepare an oral on a newspaper article, investigative report or editorial: research the topic, organise material with examples and prepare an introduction and conclusion. Learners read such texts for key features.

Learners apply reading strategies including summarising, inferring meaning and identifying manipulative language, then write a magazine article, investigative report or editorial. Task 3: Response to Texts, 60 marks.

Learners listen to a prepared speech by a former president or influential person and discuss its features and language use. Learners discuss the folktale, retell sections and practise turn-taking and defending a position.

Learners read a speech for comprehension, analysing emotive language, the introduction and conclusion, and how language shapes values. Learners write a speech using process writing, with paragraph conventions and formal style.

Learners do listening comprehension from the novel and read an extract aloud. Teach its features and conventions and how textual, punctuation and graphic cues unlock unfamiliar words. Introduce character, plot and setting.

Learners apply comprehension strategies: purpose and target group, inference, fact against opinion and implied meaning. Learners write a summary of one chapter and a descriptive essay on the novel, following the writing process.

Learners listen to a dialogue on a social issue and take notes. Teach language and power, tone and mood. Learners examine a recorded speech on a social issue for its key features, language use, format and role players.

Teach poetry: figures of speech, rhyme, rhythm, stanzas, typography, figurative meaning, mood and theme. Learners write a dialogue with correct format, order and cohesion. Task 1 Oral (reading aloud, 20 marks) is completed.

Learners do listening comprehension on a non-fictional text such as a newspaper article, then hold a group or panel discussion explaining the author's point of view with appropriate language, style and register.

Learners read a newspaper article for comprehension, distinguishing fact from opinion and summarising. Introduce folktales. Learners write a review of the article with correct format, paragraph conventions, style and register.

Learners watch an advertisement and discuss tone, pacing, emotive and manipulative language, font size, body language and the AIDA principles, then present orally on it, recording main and supporting ideas in notes.

Learners read a visual or multimedia text such as an advertisement or poster, inferring meaning and noting how visuals strengthen the message, then design one. Task 4: Writing, transactional, 10 marks, before the June test.

Task 5: June controlled test, Response to Texts (60 marks): literary or non-literary text, visual text, summary, and language structures and conventions. Learners write the test as one sitting across weeks 9 and 10.
Learners complete the June controlled test (Task 5, Response to Texts, 60 marks) and consolidate the term's reading, writing and language structures and conventions work, as the ATP gives it.

Learners listen to an informative text, noting presentation, language use, tempo and voice projection, then choose, plan and present a story. Learners read sections of the short story aloud with enunciation and pace.

Teach the short story's character, dialogue, plot, conflict, setting and theme, and a poem's internal and external structure. Learners write a short story with correct format and cohesion, following the writing process.

Learners take part in a discussion on the project: define research, create eight to ten research questions and note the instructions and stages. Introduce a drama or play: character, action, dialogue, plot, conflict and theme.

Learners read for information on the chosen topic and genre and select research to bring to school, organising it with graphic organisers, mind maps or infographics. Task 6, Creative Writing Project Stage 1: Research, 20 marks.
Teach a group discussion on the literature project covering methodology, purpose, approach and expectations. Learners read for information on the layout of the different project topics and items.

Teach a revision of the genres and text types covered in Terms 1 and 2. Learners write up the project with correct format, organised content, paragraph conventions and cohesion. Task 6 Stage 2: Writing, 30 marks.

Learners prepare the oral presentation of the project topic, and listen to and discuss current news from newspapers and magazines, noting tone, pace, intonation and persuasive language. Introduce the project rubrics.

Learners read visual and written texts, making predictions and inferring meaning, then write summary and presentation notes for the oral component. Task 7: Oral presentation of the project, 20 marks, concluded in Term 4.

Learners watch and discuss a visual, audio-visual or multimedia text, identifying main and supporting ideas and persuasive techniques, and present the project orally with attention to pronunciation, body language and resources.

Learners read a diary entry for format, purpose and cohesion, then write a diary entry on the multimedia text. Task 8: Response to Texts, 30 marks: poem 10, drama or novel 10, short stories or folklore 10.

Learners do listening comprehension on instructions and directions, taking notes and answering questions, then practise giving directions using the imperative and the second person, referring to distance and landmarks.

Learners read information texts with visuals such as maps, graphs and infographics, and a short story for its key features, then write an instructional text. Task 7, the project oral (20 marks), is completed this term.

Learners listen to a panel discussing current news, noting tone, pace, intonation, persuasive language and body language, and do prepared or unprepared reading aloud of a newspaper article, observing punctuation for effect.

Learners read newspaper and magazine articles and written speeches for main ideas, facts, opinions and figures of speech, and read a drama for plot, characterisation and dramatic irony. Learners write a newspaper article.

Learners do an oral on filling out a questionnaire or form: research the topic, organise material with examples and prepare an introduction and conclusion. Learners do listening comprehension on a form and take notes.

Learners read a questionnaire or form for key features, format and language use. Teach a poem's structure, figurative meaning, mood and theme. Task 9: Writing, transactional, 10 marks, before the end-of-year examination.
Teach examination preparation in speaking and listening: conversation, panel discussion, unprepared speech and listening comprehension. Learners revise word level and sentence level work.

Teach examination preparation in reading and writing: comprehension, summary, visual literacy, poetry, short story, drama, essays and transactional texts. Learners revise word meaning, punctuation and spelling.

Task 10: end-of-year examination, Response to Texts, Paper 2 (60 marks): literary or non-literary text, visual text, summary, and language structures and conventions. Learners write the paper as one sitting across weeks 9 and 10.

Learners complete the end-of-year examination (Task 10, Response to Texts, Paper 2, 60 marks) and consolidate the year's reading, writing and language structures and conventions work, as the ATP gives it.
